title: Superflow vs Pastel
kicker: · SUPERFLOW VS PASTEL · THE AI QA REVIEWER FOR AGENCIES
headline: Pastel is a feedback tool. Superflow is a feedback tool + a team.
secondary: The team is AI agents, built from your QA checklist. They check every site change and pin what they find. Your team decides. Your client approves from a link.
prevents: Stop finding every mistake by hand.
No more starting each round from a blank canvas.
qualifier: If your agency reviews client sites in Pastel, this page is for you.
heroCaption: It's like Pastel hired a QA team.

dimensions.label: Who checks the site
dimensions.framing: Pastel was built before AI could check a site.
leftFacts: Agents run your checklist. Every change, desktop and mobile.
Findings land as pinned comments, rationale attached.
rightFacts: A person finds every issue, then pins a comment on the canvas.
No AI features found on the vendor site.
dimensions.verdict: A canvas is a record of what a person already caught. That's the part Superflow removes.

dimensions.label: How the client says yes
dimensions.framing: Feedback is easy to collect. A yes is harder.
leftFacts: Multi-step review flows: agents check, your team gates, then the client.
Your client opens a link and taps Approve. No account, no login, no app, from their phone.
rightFacts: Guests comment with no account and no login, unlimited on every plan.
A real approval gate, even: the Finish Review button lets anyone approve or request changes, tied to a canvas version.
dimensions.verdict: Both have a recorded yes, not just a comment thread. The gate itself is even.

dimensions.label: Where you review
dimensions.framing: Half of client work lives behind a password.
leftFacts: Superflow lives on the site itself: passwords, Okta, SSO, no extension needed, guests included.
rightFacts: Both review the live site, even: Pastel serves it through its own proxy in a canvas, not a snapshot. It auto-updates when the site changes.
Private and password-protected sites work by logging in through Browse mode. No extension needed.
dimensions.verdict: Both review the live site. Pastel routes it through a proxy; Superflow lives on the page itself. Behind logins, both work, said plainly.

dimensions.label: What stays private
dimensions.framing: Your team needs somewhere to disagree.
leftFacts: Internal-only notes your team sees and the client never does.
The debate stays private; the client sees one settled answer.
rightFacts: Private, team-only comments, even: listed from the Free plan up.
dimensions.verdict: Both give your team a place to disagree before the client sees a settled answer. Call it even.

dimensions.label: What gets captured
dimensions.framing: Both tools pin. The difference is what gets attached without asking.
leftFacts: Element and text pins, area comments.
A screenshot attaches to every comment automatically.
Recordings: screen, video, voice, from the toolbar.
rightFacts: An automatic screenshot attaches to every comment too, even, plus browser type and screen size. OS in captured metadata: not yet verified.
Video Canvases add timestamped comments on uploaded video files.
Screen or session recording of a reviewer's own screen: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: Auto-capture is even; both attach proof without asking. Superflow records the reviewer's screen, voice, and video from the toolbar; Pastel reviews video you upload, and recording your own screen there is not yet verified.

dimensions.label: What it remembers
dimensions.framing: Boards hold tasks. They don't accumulate a client.
leftFacts: Brand rules and past decisions, learned once, fed to the agents next project.
rightFacts: No memory concept in product. Each canvas starts blank, and approvals reset on every new version.
dimensions.verdict: The tenth project should not start like the first, and the approval shouldn't reset either.

dimensions.label: How it fits your stack
dimensions.framing: The fix still has to ship.
leftFacts: Two-way Asana, Monday, ClickUp. Slack built in.
rightFacts: Export comments to Trello, Monday.com, Asana, Jira, a custom webhook, or Zapier, gated to the Team plan ($119/mo).
Each export carries text, metadata, screenshot, and a link back. Two-way status sync: not yet verified; the export itself is one-way.
dimensions.verdict: Pastel's exports are real but one-way and gated to its Team plan. Superflow syncs two-way from the plan you're already on.

scorecard.label: What it costs
scorecard.leftCell: Free $0 / Pro $35 / Team $119 / Enterprise $450 per month (July 2026)

pricingCompetitor: Verified July 2026: Free $0 / Pro $35 / Team $119 / Enterprise $450 per month. Team starts at 5 users, $24 per extra user monthly. Enterprise starts at 10 users, $45 per extra user monthly. Annual billing saves 17%. 14-day trial, no card. Unlimited guest reviewers on every plan.
switchingLines: One snippet on any site; one click on Webflow, WordPress, or GTM.
Paste the checklist you already have; agents assemble from it.
Open Pastel canvases finish in Pastel. No dedicated importer from Pastel found; nothing migrates on day one.
honestCloseStrengths: Pastel earned its place. No install on your live site, no extension, no code snippet: paste a URL and share one link. The canvas stays current on its own; it is not a stale copy. The Finish Review gate is real, and every plan gets unlimited guest reviewers, free.
stayLine: If a careful human pass on a live site, plus a simple approve or request-changes sign-off, works for your studio, Pastel is a fast, low-friction fit. Stay.

faq.question: Is Superflow just Pastel with AI on top?
faq.answer: No. Pastel's canvas files what a person found; Superflow's agents do the finding. A person makes every call.

faq.question: Do the agents replace my reviewers?
faq.answer: No. Agents run the first pass. Your team, then your client, signs off.

faq.question: What happens to our Pastel canvases?
faq.answer: Finish them in Pastel. Start new work in Superflow. Nothing migrates on day one.

faq.question: Will our clients have to learn a new tool?
faq.answer: No. They get a link and an Approve button. No account, no login, no app, from their phone.

faq.question: We export from Pastel to Trello or Asana.
faq.answer: Superflow syncs two-way with Asana, Monday, and ClickUp, plus webhooks and a REST API. Pastel's exports are one-way and gated to its Team plan; if you need status to flow back automatically, weigh that.
